questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was in Europe and i could take english courses, as well as reports about the academic levels of the institution.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. It was difficult to understand the course registration rules, but other than that most information was accesible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro-meeting one of my first days, but with pretty scarce information to be honest.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was recommended some facebook groups, and it seemed like it wasn't that hard, but i ended up finding housing through a personal connection. I recommend letting your own network know that you are searching, it was more common than i thought that people knew someone who knew someone etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Ask someone/research the common rent, so that you don't end up paying an obscene amount. I also lived alone, and ended up kinda regretting it. I think if you live on campus/in dorms with other students in some way, it's a little easier getting to know people and being social without it being very demanding.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I first of all had to find courses that correlated with my mandatory courses at KU, which was very very hard. Especially cause the courses of the coming semester weren't out yet, so i just had to kinda guess based of last years courses, and a lot of them ended up not being there in the end, so it was pretty much a waste of time. Besides that there was not a lot of course information, so i had to email most of my professors. Uni Wien also has a system where you don't know whether you will get a spot on a course up until the last minute (actually not until the start of the semester). This really stressed me out, but i would recommend writing your teachers and explaining them your situation if you're stressed about it, a good handful of my teachers made exceptions for me because of my exchange situation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write my mobility coordinator, but to be honest she was not to much help. I had to spend a lot of hours figuring it out myself by writing emails to teachers, looking at the uni website, asking the administration etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up actually getting all the classes that i needed. It just took a lot of work and time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start researching classes before you even apply for the exchange. Don't be afraid to be very annoying and just email or call all the people you need answers from - it will help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one BA course, the rest was MA. It was mainly because there wasn't any english BA courses that correlated with the mandatory courses i had to take. The MA courses was not too difficult for a UCPH BA student, some of the courses the academic level was perhaps even lower, but that probably depends on the person and the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was different from course to course. Generally it seemed like at Uni Wien there wasn't a lot of overall "rules" or universal structure for the courses, as the demands, style etc. varied a lot. There was a lot more mandatory participation and assignments, but the readings were easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Rent was cheaper (but i was a bit lucky). Beers and coffee out is a little cheaper than CPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there was quite a lot of possibilities, but i didn't really use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure as i didn't use them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESM parties maybe.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking outside of the city, go to as many museums as possible (i loved the Albertina). Go for walks or runs at the Schönbrunn castle - there's a zoo there was well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it's not that different from Copenhagen culturally

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak to people in your classes - ask them to lunch or a coffee after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much other than shops being closed in the weekend, and people being a bit less willing to speak english. And the bike infrastructure was worse.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beautiful buildings and pretty quiet streets and public transport.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live with other people
Plan some trips before starting your exchange - time goes by fast
Don't feel bad for not being social all the time, it's also just everyday life and not a crazy vacation energy every day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The study hall at the top floor of the NIG building is nice. The coffeemachines are horrible, but you can buy cheap coffee at BILLA (supermarket).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to be very on my own. I grew a lot from it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own haha.. And doing the course registrations/administrative things. I also worked remote at my job from CPH, i kinda regret that, it took a lot of energy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
